Distribution-based covariate assessment with the Wasserstein distance

Source: R/nm_wasserstein.R
nm_wasserstein.Rd

Implements the method of Simon, Hulot and von Fabeck (2026). For each run and each covariate, the empirical Bayes estimates of one ETA (read from the .phi file) are split into two groups of subjects and compared with the 1-Wasserstein distance W and a permutation test, together with a Welch t-test for reference. A covariate that the model accounts for leaves no residual distributional signal in the ETA: comparing a base and a final model shows whether the signal has been removed. A Wasserstein-based R2 (R2W) compares the distance of each run's ETA distribution to 0 with the one of a reference run.

Usage

nm_wasserstein(
  runs,
  covariates,
  eta = "CL",
  data = NULL,
  ref = 1,
  n_perm = 10000L,
  seed = 2025L,
  max_levels = 5L,
  continuous = c("extremes", "pairwise")
)

# S3 method for class 'nm_wasserstein'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

runs

Character vector of run directories (.reg, .nm7 or any directory holding the .phi file) or run path prefixes. Names, if any, are used as labels; otherwise the run names are used.

covariates

Character vector of covariate columns of the data set.

eta

The ETA to analyse: a PK parameter name (e.g. "CL", identified from the control stream with nm_identify_parameters()), "ETA(n)" or an integer index.

data

Covariate data: a data.frame or the path of a CSV file with an ID column (one row per subject is kept, the first one). If NULL (default), the data set named in $DATA of the first run's control stream is read.

ref

Reference run for R2W: index or label (default 1).

n_perm

Number of permutations (default 10000).

seed

Random seed for the permutation tests (default 2025). Each test uses seed + k, so results are reproducible and independent of the order of the other tests. The user's random state is restored.

max_levels

A numeric covariate with at most this many distinct values is treated as categorical (default 5).

continuous

How continuous covariates are split into quartiles (defined once on the subjects of the covariate data): "extremes" (default) compares the highest quartile Q4 with the lowest Q1; "pairwise" compares every pair of quartiles (6 comparisons), as in the pairwise analysis of the original article. Adjusted p-values (p_W_adj, p_t_adj) use the Bonferroni correction over the comparisons of the same covariate within a run.

x

An nm_wasserstein object.

...

Ignored.

Value

An object of class nm_wasserstein, a list with:

tests

one row per run x covariate comparison: run, covariate, type, comparison, n_1, n_0, W, p_W, t_stat, p_t, and the Bonferroni-adjusted p_W_adj and p_t_adj (equal to p_W and p_t when a covariate gives a single comparison).

r2w

one row per run: run, eta, n, W_to_zero, R2W (1 - W_to_zero / W_to_zero[ref]), omega and shrinkage_pct (eta-shrinkage 1 - sd(EBE)/sqrt(omega), when the .ext is found). A large difference in shrinkage between runs can make the ETA distribution narrower without any real gain.

data

the EBE merged with the comparison groups (long format), used by plot.nm_wasserstein().

settings

the arguments used.

References

Simon N, Hulot JS, von Fabeck K. Distribution-based covariate assessment using Wasserstein distance in population pharmacokinetic models. Front Pharmacol. 2026;17:1804989. doi:10.3389/fphar.2026.1804989

See also

nm_identify_parameters(), nm_compare()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
w <- nm_wasserstein(
  runs       = c(BASE = "C:/nm76g64/run/mtx/base.reg",
                 FINAL = "C:/nm76g64/run/mtx/final.reg"),
  covariates = c("CLCR", "CT01"),
  eta        = "CL"
)
w                      # tests and R2W
plot(w)                # ECDF of the ETA by group, per run and covariate
plot(w, type = "r2w")  # Wasserstein-based R2

# All pairs of CLCR quartiles, with Bonferroni-adjusted p-values
wp <- nm_wasserstein(c(BASE = "base.reg", FINAL = "final.reg"),
                     covariates = "CLCR", eta = "CL", continuous = "pairwise")
wp$tests
} # }
